gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-graduate: Bruno Ace draws every line like it was run along a ruler, with counters that stay open to the outside. Graduate, a serif with generous spacing between letters, reads dignified and unhurried.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-line-seed-jp: LINE Seed JP reads friendly and straightforward, its counters easy to slip in and out of. Bruno Ace gives it a ruler-drawn, one-character-per-beat heading, and the two stay clearly apart.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-sour-gummy: Bruno Ace looks like glass tubing bent into letters. Sour Gummy, a sans with wide gaps that keep small text crisp, stays quiet beneath it and lets the heading do the talking.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-special-gothic: Special Gothic reads soft and inviting, with rounded letters that stay open. Shrink Bruno Ace, with its plain stencil-brush line, and it loses presence fast, while the body font holds up at any size.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-gf-sura: Wide, curving, unthinning shapes up top, then a calm turn. Sura, a serif with slightly thinner hairlines and terminals that never close in, makes extended reading feel traditional and authoritative.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-cairo-play: Bruno Ace SC has a wire-like skeleton, spaced like beads on a thread. It excels at making a striking statement, while Cairo Play, a sans-serif with open round letters, stays legible when small.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-carme: Bruno Ace SC spreads its open-aperture letters out like beads on a long thread. Carme, a plain sans with a spaghetti-like line, slips in beneath and gives the page somewhere to rest.
gen-gf-bubbler-one-fs-literata: Literata reads bookish and sophisticated, with sturdy thin lines and slightly heavier thick ones. Bubbler One does the modern, snug-packed headline work, while Literata handles the sustained reading.
gen-gf-cabin-sketch-fs-fira-sans: Cabin Sketch has stout, pipe-cleaner strokes and tall little letters, like pen-nib bowls pressed flat. Fira Sans, a sans with a larger x-height, reads clean and sure over many lines.
gen-gf-cabin-sketch-rubik: Rubik brings big lowercase letters and soft, open rounds. Cabin Sketch is best at bold, uninterrupted monoline strokes, while Rubik, a plain sans, is best at staying clear in small text.
